entries.prompt:
The image is a 4 by 4 grid of sixteen separate square photographs, four rows and four columns, of equal size, edge to edge with no gutter, no border, no caption and no number. The sixteen panels are identical in exposure, white balance, background tone, camera height and subject scale, as if shot in one session on one set.

Studio still-life photography contact sheet. Every panel shares one identical setup: seamless matte light-grey cyclorama background, flat pale neutral grey about one stop below white, a touch lighter at the top, no seam between floor and wall, no horizon. One large softbox key at 45 degrees camera-left and 30 degrees above, one white bounce card camera-right for a soft open shadow side, neutral 5600K daylight, no coloured light. All objects are matte plaster, either chalk white, mid grey or graphite, with no gloss, no colour and no texture beyond a faint chalky grain. 85mm lens at f/8, camera at the height of the object mid-point so each object is seen very slightly from below and reads as solid. In every panel the object is centred, fills 70 percent of that panel width, has clear space beneath it, and carries exactly one soft feathered contact shadow directly under it. Sharp focus front to back, material texture clearly visible, matte surfaces stay matte.

a single matte chalk white plaster sphere with a faintly chalky surface. One subject alone in the panel, three-quarter view, its most characteristic face towards the camera.
